newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish Nafta Polska gains hold of Glimar refinery.
newsitem.headline: Polish Nafta Polska gains hold of Glimar refinery.

text.p: The Polish state treasury has given state-owned oil holding Nafta Polska SA control of 75 percent of the shares in small refinery Rafineria Nafty Glimar SA, Nafta Polska's spokesman said on Wednesday.
Janusz Kwiatkowski told Reuters that the deal was carried out by a Nafta Polska capital rise in which the treasury took all shares in return for the 75-percent Glimar stake.
After the deal Nafta would have 75-percent stakes in all of Poland's seven refineries.
The capital raise of 44.4 million zlotys would lift Nafta Polska's share capital to 2.9 billion zlotys.
Nafta Polska was created last year to supervise the oil sector's modernisation and privatisation. The holding is planning to sell minority stakes in the seven refineries by the end of the year.
Investors in the refineries would be given access to the lucrative network of state-owned petrol distributor CPN SA as an incentive. CPN controls nearly 1,400 of Poland's 4,700 petrol stations.
Investors would be entitled to increase their stakes in the refineries beyond 50 percent after implementing investment programmes.
